newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends at 4.0 pct, gilts extend gains.
newsitem.headline: India call ends at 4.0 pct, gilts extend gains.

text.p: Indian call money moved up slightly in afternoon trade on Tuesday to end around 4.0 percent, off the day's low of 3.5 percent, but down from Monday's close of 4.75-5.25 percent, dealers said.
They said call money firmed up marginally on late deamnd from some banks which had kept open positions.

"A few banks were uncovered and there was some some deamnd after the afternoon clearing of cheques," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But rates did not rise much...a maximum of 50 basis points from the morning's low."
Most of the day's trade was in a 3.5-4.0 percent range, he said.
Many dealers said call money will trade between 3.5 and 4.0 percent on Wednesday, but some put the range lower at between 3.0 and 3.5 percent.
Dealers said government securities ended up from Monday's close, driven by demand funded by easy call money.
"Prices went up across the board for all tenures," said one dealer at a state-run bank. "In general, prices were up at least 20-25 paise (0.20-0.25 rupee)."
The 12.59 percent 2004 stock rose to end at 104.30 rupees from the morning's 104.14. It traded on Monday at 103.70-103.84.
The 11.83 percent 2003 ended at 101.30 against Monday's 101.10, dealers said.
The 13.05 percent 2007 long bond traded at 106.57 against Monday's 106.04-106.12.
Among other stocks which posted strong gains, the 12 percent 1999 ended at 104.80, up from the morning's 104.50.
Dealers said trade in treasury bills was moderate with the 91-day bill maturing on October 18 yielding 6.40-6.50 percent.
Prices are expected to remain firm, dealers said.
"In general prices are still up in trades for tomorrow value," said a dealer. "Trade should be active tomorrow."
